evidence.quote: Results for the earnings persistence regression: Earningst+1 1⁄4 a+b Earningst+e.
Table3 panels A(full sample), B(highest earnings-volatility quintile), C(lowest quintile) each display five regressions: Earnings_(t+h)=alpha+beta*Earnings_t, h=1,2,3,4,5.

estimation_procedure.description: The source estimates the earnings-persistence equation repeatedly across horizons h=1–5. Table 2 Panel B reports separate fits in all five earnings-volatility quintiles; Table 3 reports each horizon for the full sample and the highest- and lowest-volatility quintiles. Table 3 per-fit observation counts for horizons 1–5 are full sample [9,102; 7,502; 6,147; 5,011; 4,032], highest quintile [1,682; 1,314; 1,029; 822; 659], and lowest quintile [1,899; 1,620; 1,365; 1,140; 922]. Table 2 Panel A’s full-sample h=1 fit is the same fit as Table 3 Panel A at h=1. Table 2 tests the Q1–Q5 persistence difference with a simple t-test from a pooled Q1/Q5 regression including a Q5 intercept dummy and an Earnings_t-by-Q5 slope term; adjusted-R² differences use 1,000 simulated pseudo-quintile splits. These are inference procedures, not extra baseline outcomes.
grouping_variables: Earnings-volatility population: full sample or volatility quintile (Table 2 uses all five quintiles; Table 3 reports full sample and the extreme quintiles)

evidence.quote: We use the first sub-sample (observations 1⁄4 11,061) for a comprehensive exploratory analysis of the predictive power of earnings volatility for earnings predictability
Panel B of Table 2 presents the results for quintiles formed on volatility of earnings.
The test for difference in persistence is a simple t-test from a regression that combines quintiles 1 and 5 observations, with dummy intercept and slope variables for quintile 5 observations.
We repeat this procedure 1000 times, yielding a 1000-observation empirical distribution of R <sup>2</sup> differences under the null.
In investigating the effect of earnings volatility, for parsimony we focus the presentation on the extreme quintiles.
Table3 panels A(full sample), B(highest earnings-volatility quintile), C(lowest quintile) each display five regressions: Earnings_(t+h)=alpha+beta*Earnings_t, h=1,2,3,4,5.

Number-of-observation rows for h1..5 respectively: A=[9102,7502,6147,5011,4032]; B=[1682,1314,1029,822,659]; C=[1899,1620,1365,1140,922]. These are reported counts for the corresponding horizon/group fits, not a single N to use for every grouped fit.

preprocessing.description: Earnings is deflated by average total assets. The source truncates the top and bottom 1% of earnings, accruals, and CFO in sample construction. Earnings-volatility groups use the firm-specific standard deviation of deflated earnings over the most recent five years.

evidence.quote: Earnings, accruals and cash flow from operations (CFO) are deflated using average assets.
To avoid the influence of extreme observations, we truncate the top and bottom 1% of earnings, accruals and cash flows from operations.
Vol(Earnings) is defined as the firm-specific standard deviation of Earnings over the most recent 5 years.

scope.quote: The empirical specifications focus on establishing the relation between earnings volatility and short- and long-term earnings predictability.
Table 2 presents the persistence coefficients and R <sup>2</sup> of regressions of 1-year-ahead earnings on current earnings.
Table 3 presents results for 5-year-ahead prediction of earnings, conditional on earnings volatility.

equation.quote: Results for the earnings persistence regression: Earningst+1 1⁄4 a+b Earningst+e.
Table3 panels A(full sample), B(highest earnings-volatility quintile), C(lowest quintile) each display five regressions: Earnings_(t+h)=alpha+beta*Earnings_t, h=1,2,3,4,5.

sample.quote: Firms in the full sample are randomly assigned into two sub-samples. We use the first sub-sample (observations 1⁄4 11,061) for a comprehensive exploratory analysis of the predictive power of earnings volatility for earnings predictability
After all requirements, the final sample includes 22,113 firm-years over 1988–2004.

Number-of-observation rows for h1..5 respectively: A=[9102,7502,6147,5011,4032]; B=[1682,1314,1029,822,659]; C=[1899,1620,1365,1140,922]. These are reported counts for the corresponding horizon/group fits, not a single N to use for every grouped fit.

missing_fields.method: The source does not identify the estimator actually used for the principal Table 2 and Table 3 regression applications.
missing_fields.sample_size: This entry represents fits across horizons and groups, so the scalar is null. Table 3 reports the per-fit counts listed in the estimation procedure; Table 2 Panel B does not report per-quintile N in the supplied reading.

results_missing_fields.intercept: The equations include an intercept α, but the selected Table 2 and Table 3 panels do not report its estimate.
results_missing_fields.standard_error: Individual standard errors are not printed; the tables report only that each persistence coefficient is significant at the 0.001 level.
results_missing_fields.t_statistic: Individual coefficient t-statistics are not reported; degrees of freedom and the reference distribution for the blanket coefficient significance statement are unspecified.
results_missing_fields.table2_panelB_middle_quintile_N: Table 2 Panel B does not report per-quintile observation counts; Table 3 supplies h=1 counts for the full sample and extreme quintiles only.
results_missing_fields.estimator: The paper reports regressions but does not identify the estimator used for the principal Table 2 and Table 3 fits.
results_missing_fields.fixed_effects: Fixed effects are not specified for the selected principal Table 2 and Table 3 fits.

results_review_notes: Table 2 Panel A and Table 3 Panel A h=1 report the same full-sample fit; Table 2 Panel B Q1 and Q5 h=1 likewise duplicate Table 3 Panels C and B. Duplicate locations are attached to one result set per fit.
The one-year Table 2 Panel B Q2–Q4 coefficients are reported without per-quintile sample counts. Table 3 reports per-horizon counts for the full sample and extreme quintiles only.

Per-fit adjusted R-squared values remain fit summaries outside this coefficient-focused enrichment; the printed Q1−Q5 adjusted-R-squared difference and p-value are retained as an auxiliary comparison on vol_q1_h1, with vol_q5_h1 as counterpart.
The Table 1 Vol(Earnings) row describes the sample-grouping variable, not a retained equation variable, so it is not linked to Earnings_t or a future-earnings outcome.

review_notes: The source-selected principal question is the relation between earnings volatility and short- and long-term earnings predictability (abstract/introduction and Sections 3.2–3.3). Table 2 Panel B and Table 3 are one repeated earnings-on-earnings regression family across volatility groups and horizons; duplicated full-sample one-year fits are represented once. Table 4 is retained separately because its dependent variable is the five-year sum of future earnings.

Analyst-forecast-error analyses are later Section 5 tests of users’ understanding, while accrual, earnings-level, CFO-volatility and later robustness analyses are comparison or supplemental tests; they are outside the selected principal family.
The estimator for the principal regression applications remains unreported in the supplied source. This is the unresolved issue keeping status at needs_review.
results_review_notes: Only the two frozen baseline model families are extracted: one-year persistence across volatility quintiles and horizons 1–5 for the full and extreme-quintile samples, plus the five-year summed-earnings regression in Table 4 Panels A–C. Later robustness, portfolio, analyst-forecast, and additional tests are outside scope.

Per-fit adjusted R-squared values remain model-fit summaries outside this coefficient-focused enrichment. The Table 2 Q1−Q5 and Table 4 difference-from-Panel-B adjusted-R-squared summaries and p-values are retained as auxiliary comparisons on existing fits, with named counterparts.

The Table 1 Panel B Earnings row is a broader-sample descriptive of current-year Earnings_t. Vol(Earnings) is a sample-grouping variable, not a retained equation predictor; it is not linked to Earnings_t or a future-earnings outcome. Table 1 does not provide a separate summary for the future-earnings outcomes.
The Table 4 persistence-difference method conflict is preserved: its note says bootstrap while page 11 prose says t-test. The method, reference, tail, df, and subtraction order remain unresolved.
